title: Irregular past participles
goal: Use the participles of -ir and -re verbs and the key irregular ones (fait, pris, vu, eu, été, bu, lu, mis, dit, écrit, ouvert) to tell what you did.

items.en: past participles of regular -ir and -re verbs

drills.en: I finished my report at midnight.

drills.text: Nous avons ___ le bus vingt minutes. (attendre)
drills.en: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.

items.fr: fait, pris, vu, eu, été, bu, lu, mis, dit, écrit, ouvert

drills.explain: faire → fait, with a silent t.

drills.prompt: How do you say “I saw Camille”?

accept: J'ai eu une réunion.
J'ai eu un meeting.
drills.explain: avoir → eu: [[j'ai eu]] = I had. The u sounds like the French u in tu.

items.fr: J'ai fait une randonnée au mont Royal.
items.en: I went hiking on Mount Royal.

J'ai fait une randonnée sur le mont Royal.

J'ai fait de la randonnée sur le mont Royal.

On a bu du chocolat chaud.

J'ai mis mon manteau d'hiver.

J'ai attendu l'autobus.

blocks.title: In the office kitchen, at lunchtime
blocks.context: Mei and Olivier eat lunch together on Monday. In Québec, lunch is often called le dîner.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Mei, tu as l'air fatiguée ! Ça a été, ta fin de semaine ?
lines.en: Mei, you look tired! How did your weekend go?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Oui, mais j'ai été très occupée. Vendredi soir, j'ai fini mon rapport à minuit ! Après, j'ai pris un bain et j'ai lu un peu.
lines.en: Yes, but I was very busy. On Friday evening, I finished my report at midnight! Afterwards I took a bath and read a bit.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Pauvre toi ! Moi, samedi, j'ai vu le nouveau film de Denis Villeneuve avec ma blonde.
lines.en: Poor you! On Saturday, I saw the new Denis Villeneuve film with my girlfriend.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Dimanche, il a fait beau, alors on a fait une randonnée au mont Royal. Après, on a bu un chocolat chaud et on a mis les photos sur Instagram.
lines.en: On Sunday the weather was nice, so we went hiking on Mount Royal. Afterwards we had a hot chocolate and put the photos on Instagram.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Moi, dimanche, j'ai eu un appel vidéo avec ma famille à Shanghai. Ma mère a dit : « Tu as écrit à ta grand-mère ? » Alors, j'ai écrit une longue lettre.
lines.en: On Sunday, I had a video call with my family in Shanghai. My mother said: “Have you written to your grandmother?” So I wrote a long letter.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: C'est gentil. Bon, tu as fini ? On a une réunion à 13 h.
lines.en: That's sweet. Right, have you finished? We have a meeting at 1 p.m.

options: She finished a report at midnight on Friday.
She saw a late movie on Saturday.
blocks.explain: [[J'ai fini mon rapport à minuit]]. Olivier is the one who went hiking and saw a movie.

blocks.prompt: What does Olivier mean by “Ça a été, ta fin de semaine ?”
blocks.explain: [[Ça a été ?]] is an everyday way to ask *How did it go?* [[été]] is the participle of être.

blocks.title: Same structure, different participles
blocks.body: The structure does not change: **avoir + participle**. What changes is the participle. There are two regular patterns besides **-er → -é**, and then a short list of irregular participles that you simply learn by heart. Good news: they are among the most used words in French, so you will hear them every day.

blocks.title: The three regular patterns
head: Infinitive ends in
Participle
Examples
rows: finir → fini, choisir → choisi, dormir → dormi
attendre → attendu, répondre → répondu, vendre → vendu, entendre → entendu
blocks.note: Remember [[J'ai attendu le bus]]: no word for *for*. And [[répondre à]]: [[J'ai répondu à Raj]].

blocks.title: The key irregular participles
head: Infinitive
Participle
Example
English
blocks.note: Families help: [[prendre → pris]], so [[apprendre → appris]] and [[comprendre → compris]]. [[mettre → mis]], [[écrire → écrit]], [[dire → dit]]: the final s or t is **silent**.

blocks.title: Group them by sound
blocks.pattern: -u: eu, bu, lu, vu · -is: pris, mis · -it: dit, écrit · -ait: fait
blocks.note: Learning them in sound groups is easier than one long list. Say them out loud: *u, bu, lu, vu*; *pri, mi*; *di, é-kri*; and *fè*.

examples.fr: On a bu un thé et on a lu le journal.
examples.en: We drank a tea and read the paper.

examples.fr: Karim a appris le français à Montréal.
Dimanche, il a fait très froid.
examples.en: On Sunday it was very cold.

blocks.title: The tricky one: j'ai eu
blocks.body:
[[eu]] is pronounced like the French **u** in [[tu]]: just one sound, *ü*. So [[j'ai eu]] sounds like *zhay-ü*.

Compare:

- [[J'ai eu]] (I had) ≠ [[J'ai vu]] (I saw) ≠ [[J'ai bu]] (I drank) ≠ [[J'ai lu]] (I read). Only the consonant changes, so listen carefully.
- [[fait]] rhymes with [[mais]]: *fè*. The t is silent.

examples.fr: J'ai eu, j'ai vu, j'ai bu, j'ai lu.
examples.en: I had, I saw, I drank, I read.

blocks.body:
- **Regularizing:** [[j'ai prendu]], [[j'ai faisé]], [[j'ai buvé]], [[j'ai lisé]], [[j'ai mettu]] do not exist. Say [[pris, fait, bu, lu, mis]].
- **Spelling the silent letter:** [[fait]] with a t, [[pris]] with an s, [[dit]] and [[écrit]] with a t. A trick for later: the feminine makes the letter heard ([[une lettre écrite]]).
- **Eu or été?** [[j'ai eu]] = I had; [[j'ai été]] = I was / I have been.
- **Fait for weather:** past weather uses [[il a fait]]: [[il a fait beau]] (it was nice), [[il a fait froid]] (it was cold).

blocks.title: Québec words in this dialogue
blocks.body:
- [[ma blonde]] = my girlfriend; [[mon chum]] = my boyfriend (or *my buddy*). Very common in Québec, informal. In France: [[ma copine]], [[mon copain]].
- [[le dîner]] = lunch in Québec (and Belgium, Switzerland). In France, [[le déjeuner]] is lunch and [[le dîner]] is dinner. In Québec, dinner is [[le souper]].
- [[Ça a été ?]] (How did it go?) is used everywhere. In Québec you will also hear [[J'ai été au cinéma]] for *I went to the movies*. This is informal speech; the standard form, [[je suis allé]], is in Unit 2.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Short participles are easy to miss. Exaggerate the first consonant.

lines.tip: eu = one sound, like tu without the t.
vu, then un: vu-un, two separate vowels.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Regular or irregular? Think of the infinitive first, then the participle.

blocks.prompt: Match each infinitive with its participle.

blocks.text: Hier soir, j'ai ___ un livre et j'ai ___ un thé. (lire, boire)
blocks.en: Last night I read a book and drank a tea.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means “It was cold on Saturday”?
optionFeedback: Weather uses faire, not être: il a fait froid.
That is the present: it is cold.
il a eu froid = he felt cold (a person).

blocks.prompt: We took the metro and we waited for the bus. (use nous)
accept: Nous avons pris le métro et nous avons attendu le bus.
Nous avons pris le métro et nous avons attendu l'autobus.
Nous avons pris le métro et attendu le bus.
Nous avons pris le métro et attendu l'autobus.
blocks.explain: pris is irregular; attendu follows the -re pattern. No word for *for* after attendre.

blocks.text: Tu as ___ ta place pour le spectacle ? (choisir)
blocks.en: Did you choose your seat for the show?

blocks.text: Ma mère a ___ : « Tu as ___ à ta grand-mère ? » (dire, écrire)
blocks.en: My mother said: “Have you written to your grandmother?”
blocks.explain: dire → dit, écrire → écrit: both end in a silent t.

blocks.prompt: I had a long day and I was sick.
accept: J'ai eu une longue journée et j'ai été malade.
blocks.explain: [[eu]] = had (avoir), [[été]] = was (être). Don't mix them up.

accept: Ils ont appris le français à Montréal.
À Montréal, ils ont appris le français.
blocks.explain: apprendre is in the prendre family: appris.

blocks.fr: Vous avez vu le match hier ?

blocks.text: Il fait chaud ! J'___ ___ la fenêtre. (ouvrir)
blocks.en: It's hot! I opened the window.
blocks.explain: ouvrir → ouvert: irregular, ends in a pronounced *r* sound + silent t.

blocks.prompt: Tell a colleague about yesterday evening or last Sunday. Use at least four different participles from this lesson.
checklist: At least four irregular or -ir/-re participles
One weather sentence: il a fait…
One drink or meal: j'ai bu / j'ai pris…
One thing you read, watched or wrote

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Dimanche, il a fait froid, alors j'ai passé la journée à la maison. J'ai lu un roman, j'ai bu beaucoup de thé et j'ai écrit à mes parents. Le soir, j'ai vu un film avec ma coloc. Et toi, tu as fait quoi ?
models.en: On Sunday it was cold, so I spent the day at home. I read a novel, drank lots of tea and wrote to my parents. In the evening, I watched a movie with my roommate. And you, what did you do?

blocks.prompt: Write a short text message to a friend about your Saturday: what the weather was like, how you got around, and three things you did.
checklist: Three different participles, at least two irregular

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Lucie ! Samedi, il a fait super beau. J'ai pris mon vélo et j'ai fait le tour du parc La Fontaine. Après, j'ai bu un café et j'ai lu le journal sur une terrasse. Et toi, tu as vu le spectacle ?
models.en: Hi Lucie! On Saturday the weather was great. I took my bike and rode around La Fontaine Park. Afterwards I had a coffee and read the paper on a patio. And you, did you see the show?

summary:
- Make participles of **-ir** verbs ([[fini]]) and **-re** verbs ([[attendu]])
- Use the key irregular participles: [[fait, pris, vu, eu, été, bu, lu, mis, dit, écrit, ouvert]]
- Talk about past weather: [[il a fait beau, il a fait froid]]
- Ask [[Ça a été ?]] (How did it go?)
